differences.what: The bridge is a bare grey concrete slab with no cafe terrace on it. The reference bridge is the hero of the shot: a dark-wood fascia carrying a centered wooden sign reading '雫テラス' with a white water-drop emblem, a thin cyan neon strip along its underside, and a timber pergola above it. The pergola frame spans the street, with string lights hung across it, glowing paper lanterns at the corners, copper patio heaters, and tables and chairs visible through the railing.
differences.where: Center of frame, the bridge spanning the street from y≈130 to y≈470 in the reference
differences.fix: Replace the grey slab with a dark wood-clad deck fascia. Add the lit '雫テラス' wood sign with the drop icon at the center, and an emissive cyan strip along the bottom edge. Build a 4-post timber pergola on the deck with 3–4 rows of warm string-light bulbs, 2 tall cylindrical lanterns on the left posts, 4–5 tall copper patio heaters with orange glow, and cafe tables and chairs behind a wooden railing.

differences.what: The bridge has thick grey support pillars standing in the road and on the left sidewalk. The reference shows no pillars at all: the underside of the bridge is a clean, slightly lit soffit with two warm downlights, and the street is visible unobstructed beneath it.
differences.where: Center-left, below the bridge; the pillars block the ほしマート storefront and the road
differences.fix: Delete the street-level pillars. Carry the bridge on the building facades at either end. Add 2 warm recessed downlights to the soffit and make it thinner and darker.

differences.what: The overall lighting is cold blue-grey and underexposed, while the reference is dominated by warm amber light. In the reference, lanterns, string lights, lit windows, stair LEDs and street lamps fill the frame with orange glow, balanced by magenta and cyan neon accents.
differences.where: Whole frame, worst on the left buildings and the bridge
differences.fix: Shift key and ambient light toward warm amber (≈2700K) and raise the exposure about 1.5 stops. Make every window on the left and right facades warm and emissive. Add strong bloom on lamps, lanterns and string lights. Keep the blue only in the deep sky and shadows.

differences.what: The road reflections are noisy, wavy, jagged ribbons over black asphalt with white speckle noise, which reads as a glitching shader. The reference road is a smooth, glossy wet surface. Its long vertical streak reflections in magenta, cyan, orange and white run straight down toward the camera, and asphalt texture stays visible between them.
differences.where: Center foreground and midground, the road surface
differences.fix: Remove the high-frequency ripple distortion and the speckle noise. Use planar or SSR reflections with roughness around 0.15–0.25 and vertical anisotropic stretching so each light source smears into a straight bright streak. Raise the reflection intensity and saturation, and keep a dark-grey asphalt albedo instead of pure black. Drop the flat puddle decal blobs.

differences.what: The rain is far too heavy and too visible: long, bright white streaks cover the whole frame, especially in the near foreground, and dominate the image. In the reference, rain is a faint fine drizzle that reads mostly as haze and surface sheen.
differences.where: Full frame, especially the upper half and the foreground
differences.fix: Cut the rain particle opacity by about 70% and shorten and thin the streaks. Fade particles close to the camera. Add light atmospheric mist and haze in the distance so the rain is felt rather than seen.

differences.what: The left staircase is a dark grey metal fire-escape with a single thin rail. In the reference it is a warm wooden stair whose step nosings are lit with warm LED strips. It has wooden side rails, potted plants and glowing paper lanterns on posts at its foot and top, and it rises up to the bridge level.
differences.fix: Retexture the stair as dark wood. Add an emissive warm strip under each tread nosing and solid wooden balustrades. Place a glowing white paper lantern with the drop emblem at the base and another at the top landing, and put potted shrubs and ferns along the bottom. Align the top landing with the bridge deck.

differences.what: The ほしマート convenience store has no sign and is half-hidden. The far-left storefront also lacks its bright orange/white/cyan stripe fascia. In the reference, the store has a large lit sign with a white background, an orange star and 'ほしマート', with an orange/cyan stripe beneath it. Its glass front is bright, with visible shelves.
differences.where: Left midground, under the stair, and the far-left edge
differences.fix: Add an emissive 'ほしマート' fascia sign with an orange star logo and an orange-over-cyan stripe band. Make the storefront glass bright and cool-white, with readable shelf products. Add the matching horizontal orange/white/cyan stripe sign band to the far-left building at about mid-height.

differences.what: The right building has green ivy but none of the defining props. Missing are the cascading purple wisteria, the maneki-neko cat on the balcony rail, and the dense red-pot flower boxes. The round red/orange paper lanterns with white emblems under the awning are also missing; the capture has only small yellow bulbs there.
differences.where: Right side: the upper facade, the balcony rail and below the blue/white awning
differences.fix: Add hanging purple wisteria clusters over the balcony and roof eaves, and also over the bridge planters. Place a white maneki-neko figurine at the right end of the balcony rail. Fill the rail with red pots of pink and red flowers. Hang 5–6 glowing orange-red chochin lanterns with white crests under the awning.

differences.what: The background is an empty purple void with a few scattered squares, crossed by sagging overhead power lines. The reference shows a dense cluster of tall skyscrapers full of lit windows, with pink and cyan neon signs, receding in blue haze above the bridge.
differences.where: Top center, the background above the bridge
differences.fix: Remove the power lines. Add a skyline of 6–10 tall tower silhouettes with emissive window grids and a few vertical neon signs, fogged with blue-purple height fog. The tops should reach near the top of the frame.

differences.what: The street lamps are thin grey poles with dim, flat heads. The cyan neon line runs as a diagonal laser across the sky instead of along the building cornice. The camera also sits too low, putting the bridge around y≈450–570 when it should span y≈130–470. In the reference, the street lamps are tall dark curved posts with bright warm glowing heads (left foreground and right of center), and the cyan neon traces the top edge of the left building.
differences.where: Left foreground lamp, right-center lamp, top-left sky; overall framing
differences.fix: Give both lamps bright warm emissive heads with bloom and a light cone onto the wet pavement. Re-route the cyan neon tube along the left building's roofline edge. Raise the camera and tilt it down slightly so the bridge and its pergola sit in the upper-middle third and the crosswalk fills the bottom edge.
